en.head: One simulator, now a complete business-case engine: operations, finance and live inputs in a single run.

items.text: The earlier standalone lab was retired and redirected. The portal now shows a single Base44 application through a scroll-safe preview that expands to full screen.
Set a business target and the solver searches operating conditions, compares candidates and stress-tests them. The search runs in a background worker, so the screen never freezes.
Tokyo, Nagoya and Toyota share scenario inputs. Staging and night-time sites can be dragged on the map, and each booking can be traced from request to pickup.
An event-driven disruption model and a customer-touchpoint model show what owning the user interface changes in dispatch and revenue.

A 50-line P/L, cash flow for 2025–2035, IRR, NPV and sensitivity are calculated from the same run as the operations. Operating cost can now be itemised: MaaS operations splits into seven components (14 component indices in the bundled baseline), and four per-vehicle cost inputs (remote monitoring, insurance, maintenance, communications) are added at a default of zero. Totals are unchanged.
A parameter registry records where each input came from, starting from the 2030 planning baseline.
Inputs are received in real time. The simulator's calculated results become the reference that the portfolio, Federation and Seneschal read.
The search proposes better operating conditions but does not change the plan by itself.
A fleet-hub study dataset is published alongside the simulator.

Quick, Standard and Detailed. Quick shows aggregated totals and four headline figures (IRR, NPV, 2035 free cash flow, payback year); Standard shows every P&L line; Detailed adds how each line is calculated and the cost mix. The model and numbers are the same in all three.

en.note: Synthetic regions and editable assumptions. Results are planning-scenario values, not operating results.

en.head: Numbers now follow the simulator, with a layout gate that refuses to let the page move.

items.text: Calculated values flow from the simulator's project-finance engine into the PDF. Inputs stay under manual control in Federation.
Only digit glyphs are exchanged inside the existing text. A rewrite that would change the character count, a sign or a glyph width, or that needs a glyph missing from the embedded font, is refused.

The result must keep the page count, character positions and fonts, show only the planned text change, and alter no pixel outside the rewritten digits. If any check fails, the previous PDF stays published.
The same verification runs automatically on each pull request and each push.
The depreciation basis now matches the investment amount, and 2035 operating profit in the plan scenario is +13.378 B JPY.

en.head: The same app, rebuilt for the real world: connected to live public data and checked against production every morning.

items.text: Japan Meteorological Agency warnings, forecasts, earthquakes, tsunami, typhoons and AMeDAS observations, plus heat index, elevation and solar radiation.
Weather appears on the calendar, disasters on a yellow alert card, and parking and charging are pulled into the schedule. Bookings are sent with congestion-aware travel time.

items.lead: Assistant proposals, applied only on approval.
items.text: The integrated AI planner turns one request into schedule options. Nothing is written to the calendar until the user approves. Events marked as fixed are not moved, an outdated proposal can no longer be approved, ending the conversation discards pending proposals while keeping approved events, and a lost response after saving does not cause a double write. Behaviour is checked by an independent evaluation ledger of 119 cases (114 pass, 0 fail, 5 inconclusive) and a use-case ledger of 31 request scenarios (13 implemented, 12 waiting on external data). Both use fixed test data, not the published app or real calendars.

The earthquake alert card offers a “consider going home or meeting” action that opens a proposal with a meeting candidate on the map. Roads of unknown condition are drawn dashed, a reported closure blocks selection, and selecting a candidate saves nothing until the normal approval step. It runs on demonstration data kept separate from normal events.

Electricity supply–demand now covers all nine grid areas (from one), and the traffic API of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism is added. If no station is near, the search radius widens from about 3 km to 8 km. The yellow card also shows power-usage rate and heat index at severe level or above.

items.lead: Two-way Google Calendar sync, no login.
items.text: A public sample calendar syncs both ways, driven by change notifications with a retry queue, so nothing is lost.
Square results join the search suggestions as read-only.
Every write operation, including bookings, is tested on each pull request and again every morning against the live app in a real Chrome.
The assistant, Federation console, wallet QR, side menu and the 250 KB English dictionary now load only when needed.

280+ unreachable components, logic and unused packages were deleted behind behaviour-parity tests and before/after screen comparison. Backend functions no longer expose secrets, map overlay HTML is escaped, and the blank clinic screen was replaced by a step-by-step intake flow.

en.note: Prototype with demonstration data where noted in the app. External-data features use free public APIs.

en.head: Federation now proves its own numbers: one source of truth, a profitability gate, and cards that are scored and independently reviewed.

items.text: The simulator's project-finance engine is now the reference for calculated results. Indices stay in Federation and flow out in real time.
A 50-line P/L, cash flow for 2025–2035, IRR, NPV and sensitivity are calculated and fed back to the portfolio.
A 2035 profit can be shown only after full-system verification: revenue must reconcile with operating scale, and depreciation must be explainable from total investment and useful life.
Depreciation was rebased on the investment amount; 2035 operating profit in the plan scenario is +13.378 B JPY.
A search for the most profitable conditions runs in the simulator and proposes changes without overwriting the plan.
Outside data is gathered into dated proposals to update indices (latest 19 Oct), for a person to approve.
Blueprint and Artifact cards are scored continuously. Six rounds of independent review are recorded in a ledger, covering vehicle platforms, WBS, risk register, pricing and the control structure.
An automatic check against the portfolio was introduced, and Blueprint cards were expanded to match it.
Two original-application images were transcribed and checked against the canonical numbers.
Seneschal's numeric baseline now follows Federation and the simulator results.

en.note: Planning-scenario values from editable assumptions, not operating results.
